title: Piezo-latched snap-through nanobeam holds bits as mechanical buckling
idea: Effect walk: piezoelectricity + Euler buckling. A 200-nm AlN/Si bimorph beam is built pre-compressed so it rests in one of two buckled states (up or down); a +/-1 V piezo pulse snaps it through in ~ns, and a monolayer MoS2 strain gauge at the beam root reads the state non-destructively by piezoresistance.
why: The bit sits behind an elastic energy barrier (>100 kT), not a charge, so there is no leakage tail or refresh (fact 3), no capacitor (fact 1) and no row-hammer coupling (fact 9); beams stack in BEOL without EUV, though pitch is ~4-8F per layer.

title: Redox pseudocapacitor nanocell replaces 70:1 pillar with planar charge sponge
idea: Effect walk: Faradaic surface redox (pseudocapacitance). Replace the dielectric capacitor with a 5-nm hydrous RuO2 or Ti3C2 MXene film against a nanometre solid proton conductor; fast surface redox stores ~100-1000 uF/cm2 versus ~7 uF/cm2 for ZrO2, so a flat 30x30 nm pad holds ~4-5 fF at 0.5 V.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) with no AR 60-75 etch, removing the deep-etch/deposition module (~30-50% of capacitor cost); risks are self-discharge and whether surface redox keeps up at ns timescales.

title: Charge-gated Mott channel amplifies a few hundred stored electrons
idea: Effect walk: filling-controlled Mott transition. The storage node gates a 3-nm channel of a correlated oxide (strained NdNiO3 or electron-doped Sr2IrO4) poised at its metal-insulator boundary, so a few hundred stored electrons (~0.1-0.3 e per unit cell under a 100 nm2 gate) swing channel resistance ~100x for a gain read.
why: Cuts required storage charge ~100x (5 fF to ~0.03-0.05 fF), removing the high-AR capacitor (fact 1) and shrinking the cell toward 4F2; risks are retaining so few electrons against the leakage tail and Mott-channel variability.

title: Proton-doped nickelate bit: electron filling flips resistance a millionfold
idea: Effect walk: ion migration driving a Mott transition. A 10-nm SmNiO3 channel exchanges H+ with an adjacent nanometre proton reservoir; each inserted proton donates an electron that localizes on Ni (Ni3+ to Ni2+), turning the metal into a strongly correlated insulator with up to ~10^6 resistance change, read at ~50 mV.
why: Holds state without refresh (fact 3) and the enormous read margin removes full sense-amp restore (fact 8); a vertical 4F2 BEOL stack with no capacitor; proton endurance (>10^12 cycles needed) and ns kinetics are the open risks.

title: DX-centre persistent photoconductivity: light writes, lattice barrier holds
idea: Effect walk: photoconductivity with large lattice relaxation. A waveguide photon pulse ionizes DX-type deep donors in a channel (AlGaAs:Si-like centres re-engineered in a wide-gap host with a >=0.9 eV capture barrier) into shallow donors, raising conductance; the configurational barrier keeps electrons free, and a hot-electron gate pulse recaptures them to reset.
why: Holds the bit in a lattice-relaxation barrier instead of leakage-limited charge, targeting refresh-free retention (fact 3) and an optical write path that bypasses wordline drivers (fact 7); known DX hosts only retain below ~100 K, so a new host is required.

title: Spin-crossover molecular film stores bits in iron's spin state
idea: Effect walk: thermal hysteresis of spin crossover. A 5-nm film of an Fe(II)-triazole coordination polymer with a 20-40 K hysteresis loop straddling room temperature forms the dielectric of a small capacitor; a short heat or field pulse flips low-spin and high-spin, changing permittivity and volume ~10%, read as a capacitance difference with a small AC probe.
why: A bistable molecular state needs no refresh and no high-AR capacitor; solution-deposited BEOL layers stack without EUV (fact 4) and use only iron, carbon and nitrogen, no chokepoint materials; switching speed and cycling endurance are unproven at ns scale.

title: Prussian-blue electrochromic bit read by light on a photonic bus
idea: Effect walk: electrochromism. Each bit is a 50-nm Prussian-blue (iron hexacyanoferrate, tungsten-free) patch on a silicon-nitride waveguide; inserting ~10^3 K+ or H+ ions from a thin solid electrolyte bleaches or colours it, changing optical absorption, so a passing light pulse reads the bit without electrical bitlines while the coloured state holds for hours.
why: Reads memory straight onto co-packaged optics, skipping bitline CV2 and SerDes energy (fact 5, 3-20 pJ/bit) for disaggregated memory pools, with abundant iron chemistry; ion kinetics are us-class unless patches shrink to ~10 nm.

title: Orbital Hall torque from chromium writes magnets without tungsten or platinum
idea: Effect walk: orbital Hall effect. Replace W/Pt/Ta spin-Hall write lines in SOT magnetic cells with light 3d metals (Cr, Ti, V) whose orbital Hall conductivity is predicted ~10x Pt's spin Hall conductivity, converting the orbital current to torque through a 1-nm Ni or Gd conversion layer under the free layer.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and platinum from the write path and may cut write current 2-5x, making SOT-class DRAM-replacement cells cheaper in scarce-resource terms.

title: Noncollinear antiferromagnet bits pack tight with zero stray field
idea: Effect walk: spin Hall switching + anomalous Hall effect in a Weyl antiferromagnet. 10-nm Mn3Sn islands store the bit as the chirality of their triangular spin order, switched by spin-orbit torque from an adjacent line and read by the sign of the large anomalous Hall voltage they emit despite near-zero net moment.
why: Zero stray field removes inter-cell magnetic disturb so pitch can approach 2F, and dynamics reach 10-100 ps; Mn and Sn are abundant; aims at density and endurance beyond MRAM's dipolar limit.

title: Altermagnet tunnel junction: spin-split readout without net magnetization
idea: Effect walk: altermagnetic spin splitting. Build a tunnel junction whose free electrode is an altermagnet (CrSb or MnTe, avoiding Ru) with momentum-dependent spin-split bands, so the Neel vector produces a TMR-like resistance change; write by spin-orbit or current-induced Neel switching.
why: Combines ferromagnet-grade electrical readout with antiferromagnet immunity to fields and THz dynamics, enabling magnetic cells below 20-nm pitch without dipolar crosstalk and with abundant elements.

title: Twin resonant-tunneling diodes form a static bit at DRAM pitch
idea: Effect walk: resonant tunneling negative differential resistance. Two stacked double-barrier RTDs (Si/SiGe or GaN/AlN) in series form a Goto pair with two stable midpoint voltages; one access transistor writes the midpoint, and holding draws only the RTD valley current.
why: Static storage without refresh (fact 3) or capacitor (fact 1) in a vertical ~6-8F2 stack; feasible only if valley current density falls to ~1 A/cm2 (pA per cell), i.e. peak-to-valley ratio >10^4 at room temperature.

title: Ferroelectric AlScN barrier toggles GaN 2DEG for gain-read memory
idea: Effect walk: spontaneous and piezoelectric polarization in wurtzite nitrides. A 5-nm ferroelectric AlScN barrier on GaN turns the polarization-induced 2D electron gas on or off depending on its switched polarity, giving a non-destructive gain read with ~10^4 on/off and no capacitor.
why: Runs on existing U.S. GaN/AlN fabs and 150-200 mm tools (U.S. manufacturability, capital intensity), and avoids the capacitor (fact 1) and destructive read (fact 8); AlScN's 3-5 MV/cm coercive field and wake-up/fatigue are the risks.

title: Quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 makes planar storage capacitors at 77 K
idea: Effect walk: quantum paraelectricity. Below ~100 K, SrTiO3 (or KTaO3) permittivity climbs into the thousands because quantum fluctuations suppress the ferroelectric transition, so a 10-nm epitaxial film on a planar cell stores 5 fF in a small fraction of today's area; at 77 K the access-transistor leakage tail also drops by >10^6.
why: Answers the capacitor wall (fact 1 needs k~70; STO offers k~1000+ cold even after thin-film dead-layer losses) and removes refresh (fact 3) for liquid-nitrogen-cooled AI memory pools, with no AR-60 etch; cooling costs ~10 W wall power per W removed.

title: Charge-density-wave order in 1T-TaS2 holds bits as electron-crystal phase
idea: Effect walk: charge-density-wave ordering. A 10-nm 1T-TaS2 film switches between a commensurate insulating CDW and a metastable metallic 'mosaic' CDW under a ~30-ps few-volt pulse, is read by its 10-100x resistance difference, and is reverted by a longer, weaker pulse.
why: Electronic ordering switches in picoseconds with fJ-class energy and no atomic migration, promising endurance and speed in a BEOL crosspoint; the hidden state is only long-lived at cryogenic temperatures, so room-temperature analogues are needed.

title: One skyrmion per nanodisk: topological winding number as the bit
idea: Effect walk: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya chiral magnetism. A 20-nm Ta/CoFeB/MgO disk holds zero or one skyrmion; a current pulse nucleates or annihilates it at an engineered notch, and the bit is read through noncollinear magnetoresistance in a vertical tunnel stack.
why: Topological winding adds an energy barrier that does not scale with volume, so retention holds at smaller volumes than an MTJ free layer, pushing density past MRAM's thermal-stability limit.

title: Domain-inverted lithium niobate microrings store bits as optical resonance shifts
idea: Effect walk: Pockels effect sign inversion. In thin-film LiNbO3, poling a segment of a microring flips the sign of its electro-optic coefficient; under a small DC bias the ring resonance moves left or right depending on the domain, so a WDM probe reads 32 rings in parallel non-destructively and a 5-V electrode pulse rewrites the domain.
why: Puts memory directly on the optical interconnect, deleting O-E-O conversion energy (fact 5) for photonic switches and CPO buffers; area per bit is um2, so it is a photonic buffer tier rather than a DRAM substitute.

title: Layer-counted h-BN tunnel barrier dials retention like a knob
idea: Effect walk: direct quantum tunneling through atomically defined barriers. A 2D semi-floating-gate cell (graphene or MoS2 storage layer) sits behind exactly N layers of h-BN; because direct-tunneling current drops ~10x per added 0.33-nm layer, N=4-6 sets retention near 1 s while 10-ns writes use direct (not Fowler-Nordheim) tunneling at 2-3 V that creates no oxide traps.
why: Replaces junction leakage statistics with a quantized, atomically uniform barrier, collapsing the retention tail (fact 3) and refresh energy, and needs no capacitor (fact 1); wafer-scale defect-free h-BN and the write/hold current ratio of ~10^8 are the risks.

title: Buried Ge quantum well holds holes behind a band-offset wall
idea: Effect walk: heterojunction band-offset confinement. A capacitorless cell stores holes in a 5-nm compressively strained Ge quantum well beneath a Si channel; the ~0.5 eV valence-band offset, not a leaky p-n junction, is the retention barrier, and stored holes shift channel threshold for a gain read.
why: Removes the capacitor (fact 1) and attacks the junction-generation leakage tail (fact 3), allowing a 4F2 vertical cell built with SiGe epitaxy already running in U.S. fabs.

title: Recirculating GHz phonon loops revive mercury delay-line memory on chip
idea: Effect walk: piezoelectric transduction of acoustic waves. Bits are 100-ps acoustic pulses circulating in a thin-film LiNbO3-on-Si phononic waveguide loop, regenerated once per lap by a piezo transducer and amplifier; slow-wave phononic-crystal sections (group velocity <200 m/s) pack more bits per micron.
why: A lithography-light, capacitor-free store for sequential data such as KV-cache streams; density is 10-50x below DRAM unless slow-wave sections succeed, so it targets a streaming tier and capital intensity, not random access.

title: Single femtosecond pulse toggles ferrimagnet bit: light-written magnetic memory
idea: Effect walk: helicity-independent all-optical switching in ferrimagnets. A 10-nm GdFeCo (or rare-earth-free Mn-based ferrimagnet) free layer of an MTJ sits under a plasmonic nano-antenna fed by a waveguide; each ~100-fs pulse deterministically toggles magnetization through ultrafast sublattice demagnetization, and TMR reads it electrically.
why: Picosecond writes with no current through the junction (unlimited write endurance), and optical addressing removes wordline-driver periphery (fact 7); Gd supply concentration and nanoscale plasmonic coupling efficiency are the risks.

title: Antiferroelectric biased at critical field gives giant differential capacitance
idea: Effect walk: field-induced antiferroelectric-to-ferroelectric transition. A ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor is held by a built-in work-function bias just below its forward switching field, where dP/dE is 5-10x the linear permittivity, so a +/-0.3 V signal swing moves 5-fF-equivalent charge from a shallow AR~15 cylinder.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1: needs k~70 or AR~115) by borrowing a phase transition's effective k of ~150-300, permitting AR 15-25 pillars with fewer deep-etch steps; sub-loop hysteresis and fatigue are the risks.

title: Bulk photovoltaic read: polarization reports its sign as photocurrent
idea: Effect walk: bulk photovoltaic (shift-current) effect. Ferroelectric nano-capacitors (BaTiO3 or CuInP2S6) under a shared transparent electrode are flood-illuminated by a backside waveguide flash; each cell's photocurrent sign equals its polarization direction, integrated by a per-column gain stage without switching the domain.
why: Non-destructive ferroelectric read removes FeRAM's read-then-rewrite fatigue and restore energy (fact 8), letting polar cells act as working memory with unlimited reads; shift currents are small, so sensing gain is the risk.

title: Shape-memory twin variants open or close a tunnel gap
idea: Effect walk: ferroelastic martensitic twinning. A 20-nm NiTi nano-pillar has two stable twin variants whose heights differ by ~4% (~0.8 nm); a piezo or thermal pulse selects the variant, opening or closing a ~1-nm h-BN/vacuum tunnel gap above it, which changes tunneling current by up to ~10^6-10^7.
why: A crystallographic barrier holds the state with zero leakage and no refresh, and the enormous read margin enables tiny-swing reads; abundant Ni and Ti (no W); nanoscale martensite fatigue over 10^15 cycles is unknown.

title: Single-electron Coulomb-blockade node read by an on-cell SET
idea: Effect walk: Coulomb blockade. Store the bit as 0 vs ~10 electrons on a 3-nm Si dot whose ~150 meV charging energy quantizes occupancy, written through a tunnel barrier at ~0.2 V and read by a co-integrated single-electron transistor whose current swings ~100x per added electron.
why: Moves ~10 electrons instead of ~30,000 (5 fF x 1 V) and the SET gain lets the bitline swing only ~50 mV: ~100x lower cell+bitline energy per access (fact 10), and the Coulomb gap suppresses leakage (fact 3); room-temperature SET variability is the risk.

title: Sliding ferroelectric bilayer flips by interlayer slip at 0.2 V
idea: Effect walk: sliding (stacking) ferroelectricity. In a parallel-stacked h-BN or 3R-MoS2 bilayer, the out-of-plane dipole reverses when one layer slides one bond length (AB to BA) under ~0.1-0.3 V, and a graphene-contacted tunnel junction reads the ~10x tunneling-resistance change non-destructively.
why: No ion displacement across the film and ~0.2 V on an atomically thin capacitor cut write energy ~25x versus 1-V CV2, and the non-destructive read removes restore energy (fact 8); reported fatigue-free switching suits the endurance target.

title: Voltage-only magnetoelectric cell read by inverse Rashba-Edelstein voltage
idea: Effect walk: magnetoelectric coupling + spin-to-charge conversion. A 10-nm La-doped BiFeO3 film reorients its canted antiferromagnetic order at ~100 mV, dragging an exchange-coupled CoFe nanomagnet; reading passes a tiny spin current into a Bi/Ag or topological interface whose inverse Rashba-Edelstein effect outputs a voltage whose sign is the bit.
why: Write is capacitive (~10 aJ at 100 mV, no charge current) and read is non-destructive, aiming 10-100x below DRAM's fJ-class cell+bitline write and restore energy (facts 8, 10).

title: Barrier-trimmed MTJ trades ten-year retention for tenfold cheaper writes
idea: Effect walk: Neel-Arrhenius thermal activation. Design the MTJ free layer for thermal stability ~25-30 (seconds of retention at 85 C) instead of ~60 (ten years); critical current scales with the barrier, so writes need ~2-2.5x less current and, with shorter pulses, ~5-10x less energy, while a refresh every ~100 ms costs ~1% duty.
why: Turns MRAM's over-engineered retention into energy: a DRAM-class volatile cell from a mature MTJ stack at ~10x lower write energy than NVM-grade STT, with non-destructive read and no capacitor (fact 1).

title: Flux quanta in kinetic-inductance nanowire loops for cryogenic AI memory
idea: Effect walk: flux quantization in superconductors. Each bit is the presence or absence of one flux quantum in a loop of 10-nm-wide NbN or NbTiN nanowire whose large kinetic inductance shrinks the loop to ~0.1 um2; writes and reads use nanocryotron (nTron) switches instead of Josephson junctions, costing ~10^-18 J per access.
why: Access energy ~10^-18 J vs ~10^-14 J for DRAM cell+bitline: even after a ~500x 4-K cooling penalty it remains ~20x lower, giving cryogenic accelerators and quantum-control stacks a missing dense memory.

title: Ferroelectric-semiconductor channel: the transistor itself is the bit
idea: Effect walk: locked in-plane/out-of-plane ferroelectricity in a semiconductor. A 3-nm alpha-In2Se3 channel's own polarization sets its band bending and conductance; a ~0.5 V gate pulse switches the channel dipoles, and reading at 0.1 V drain bias senses a ~10^3 current ratio without disturbing polarization.
why: No separate capacitor or full-swing bitline: a 0.1-V gain read gives ~10-20x lower read energy than DRAM sensing and avoids destructive read (fact 8); indium supply concentration is a resource caveat.

title: Conducting ferroelectric domain walls as switchable nanoscale wires
idea: Effect walk: domain-wall conduction. In a thin-film LiNbO3 or ErMnO3 cell, a written charged domain wall bridging two electrodes conducts ~10^4x better than the bulk; short pulses inject or erase the wall to store the bit, and a 0.1-V read through the wall leaves polarization untouched.
why: A non-destructive 0.1-V read with large margin removes the restore cycle and full-rail bitline charging (facts 8, 10), cutting read energy >10x; the wall is ~1 nm wide, so density is set by lithography, not physics.

title: Gate voltage flips interlayer magnetic order in a 2D magnet
idea: Effect walk: electrostatic doping-tuned interlayer exchange. In bilayer CrI3-class or room-temperature Fe3GaTe2 van der Waals magnets, a ~0.1 V/nm gate field shifts interlayer exchange between antiparallel and parallel, switching a spin-filter tunnel junction resistance by >10x with a purely capacitive write.
why: No current flows through the junction during write (~aJ at sub-volt) and spin-filter read has very large TMR, so access energy can be 10-100x below DRAM; Curie temperature and air stability are the risks.

title: Chiral molecules write magnets with mere capacitor charging current
idea: Effect walk: chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS). A monolayer of helical peptides or chiral perovskite between a gate and a 1-nm Co free layer injects spin-polarized displacement current while the capacitor charges, transferring enough angular momentum to flip magnetization with no DC current; TMR reads it.
why: Write energy is only the charging energy of an aF capacitor (~aJ), 10-1000x below fJ-class DRAM or STT writes; speculative because CISS magnitudes and timescales are disputed.

title: Van der Waals stiction latch: nanoflap stays stuck until kicked
idea: Effect walk: van der Waals/Casimir adhesion. A 50-nm graphene or SiC nanoflap is pulled into contact by a ~0.5 V electrostatic pulse and held at zero power by vdW adhesion; a second electrode releases it, and a 10-mV contact-resistance check reads the state.
why: Zero hold power (no refresh), ~aJ contact reads at 10 mV and ~0.1 fJ actuation of an aF-scale gap put access energy >10x below DRAM; contact wear over >10^15 cycles is the reliability risk.

title: Polarity-encoded piezo resonators read by RF echo, never switched
idea: Effect walk: sign of the piezoelectric coefficient. Nanoscale ferroelectric AlScN contour-mode resonators store the bit as the sign of d33; a tiny RF ping on a shared line excites 64 resonators at distinct frequencies, and each response phase (0 vs 180 degrees) reveals its polarization while most stored mechanical energy returns to the line.
why: Read is resonant and reversible (Q~1000 recovers energy), non-destructive (fact 8), and reads 64 bits per ping by frequency multiplexing, giving >10x lower read energy per bit than DRAM sensing; resonator area limits density.

title: Pyroelectric read: a nanoheater asks the domain which way it points
idea: Effect walk: pyroelectricity. A 10-nm resistive nanoheater under a ferroelectric bit warms a ~20-nm volume by ~10 K for 2 ns (~0.2 fJ); the polarization-dependent pyro-current, whose sign is the bit, charges the aF sense gate of a gain transistor, so the domain is read without being switched or rewritten.
why: Replaces switch-and-restore reads and full bitline swings (facts 8, 10) with ~0.2-1 fJ of heat, ~10x below DRAM read energy per bit; the signal is only a few electrons, so sensing noise is the risk.

title: Strain-switched magnetostrictive nanomagnets written by a piezo voltage
idea: Effect walk: inverse magnetostriction (Villari effect). An elliptical 50x40 nm Co-Fe nanomagnet on an AlScN piezo layer receives a 0.2-V strain pulse that rotates its easy axis 90 degrees; releasing the strain at the precessional half-period toggles magnetization, and an MTJ reads it.
why: Capacitive strain write costs ~1 aJ-1 fJ with no current, versus ~100 fJ STT and ~10 fJ DRAM cell+bitline: >=10x lower, non-volatile so no refresh; uses Co-Fe instead of Ga- or rare-earth magnetostrictors.

title: Park VO2 inside its hysteresis loop; nudge bits with heat or strain
idea: Effect walk: thermal hysteresis of the VO2 metal-insulator transition. A strain- and dopant-engineered VO2 array (Tc ~90 C, ~15 K loop) is held at a regulated mid-loop temperature so metal and insulator are both stable; a 1-ns Joule nudge of a few kelvin writes 'metal', a piezo strain pulse that lifts the loop writes 'insulator', and the ~10^3 resistance ratio is read at 50 mV.
why: Write only supplies the latent heat of a ~10-nm volume (~0.2 fJ) plus a strain nudge, and read uses tiny bias on huge contrast: ~10x below DRAM cell+bitline energy with zero refresh, using the chip's waste heat to hold state.

title: Negative-capacitance boosted cell lets array voltage fall to 0.3 V
idea: Effect walk: ferroelectric negative capacitance. A thin, domain-stabilized ferroelectric layer in series with the storage dielectric raises the stack's effective capacitance ~3x inside the non-hysteretic NC window, so the cell stores the same signal charge at an array voltage of ~0.33 V and wordline ~1.2 V.
why: Breaks the voltage floor (fact 10): bitline CV2 scales with V2, so 1 V to 0.33 V cuts array energy per access ~9-10x while also easing the capacitor wall (fact 1); hysteresis-free NC at GHz rates is disputed.

title: Spin-wave bus reads eight nanomagnets with one multiplexed pulse
idea: Effect walk: magnon phase shift. Eight 30-nm nanomagnet bits sit along a CoFeB or garnet spin-wave waveguide, each coupled to a different resonant mode; one broadband spin-wave pulse picks up a bit-dependent phase at each frequency, and a single inductive detector demultiplexes all eight.
why: Magnons carry no charge current and one pulse reads 8-16 bits, so read energy per bit falls ~10x versus charging a bitline per bit, and it reads exactly the word needed instead of a page (fact 8).

title: Single-molecule tautomer switch: one hydrogen hop stores a bit
idea: Effect walk: proton tunneling in tautomerization. A porphycene or naphthalocyanine molecule anchored in a nanogap flips which nitrogen atoms hold its inner hydrogens when a 0.2-0.4 eV tunneling electron excites it, and its two tautomers give distinct junction conductance read at 10 mV.
why: Switching costs one vibrational excitation (~0.1 aJ) and a 10-mV, ns read through one molecule is ~10^-17 J: >=100x below DRAM, at molecular density; room-temperature stability and contact reproducibility are speculative.

title: Waste-heat Seebeck read: cells report state with no applied bias
idea: Effect walk: Seebeck effect. A phase-state cell whose two states have very different thermopower (insulator ~400 uV/K vs metal ~10 uV/K, e.g. a correlated oxide) spans the natural 1-5 K vertical gradient of the BEOL stack; selecting it connects it to a high-impedance sense gate that sees ~1 mV vs ~10 uV of thermovoltage, so the read is powered by waste heat.
why: The read draws no charge from the supply, only the select and low-swing sense gate are charged, cutting read energy ~10x and avoiding destructive read (fact 8); gradient uniformity and mV-level sensing noise are the risks.

title: Adiabatic ramped access recycles bitline charge through resonant LC tanks
idea: Effect walk: adiabatic charging, where dissipation scales as (RC/T) x CV2. Make the cell-plus-bitline part of an LC tank using 3D BEOL inductors and drive wordlines and bitlines with a resonant sinusoidal clock over 5-10 ns instead of ~0.1-ns steps, returning ~90% of the bitline charge to the tank after each access.
why: Bitline charging dominates DRAM access energy (facts 5, 8, 10); ramps with T~20 RC cut dissipation ~10x at the cost of a slightly longer row cycle, with standard materials.

title: Charge-order ferroelectric switches by electron hopping, not ion motion
idea: Effect walk: electronic ferroelectricity from charge ordering. Use a mixed-valence oxide (LuFe2O4-type, or a rare-earth-free charge-ordered ferrite or manganite) whose polarization comes from Fe2+/Fe3+ ordering, so switching moves electrons between sites rather than displacing ions, at ~meV per unit cell with no oxygen-vacancy fatigue.
why: Electron-only switching promises ~10x lower switching charge-voltage product and fatigue-free endurance for a polar storage cell; room-temperature electronic ferroelectricity in these materials is contested.

title: Read resistance states by listening to their Johnson thermal noise
idea: Effect walk: Johnson-Nyquist noise. A selected high- or low-resistance cell (e.g. 100 kOhm vs 10 MOhm) is connected unbiased to a local low-noise correlator that distinguishes the ~10x noise-voltage difference over a 20-ns window; no current is driven, so the cell is never disturbed.
why: Zero injected read energy and no read disturb: per-bit read cost becomes the amortized correlator energy, potentially ~10x below bitline-charging reads in large banks; low-power amplifiers per sense group are the hard part.

title: Nonlinear-permittivity probe reads ferroelectric bits below coercive field
idea: Effect walk: nonlinear dielectric response. The second-order permittivity of a ferroelectric is odd in polarization, so a 50-mV sinusoid far below the coercive voltage produces a second-harmonic charge whose phase flips with the bit; a local lock-in style sense stage reads it while leaving the domain untouched.
why: Turns FeRAM's destructive switch-and-restore read (full coercive CV2) into a 50-mV probe: ~10-20x lower read energy and no read fatigue (fact 8); the small signal needs fF-class cells and local sensing.

title: Quantum anomalous Hall edge chirality as a dissipationless cryogenic bit
idea: Effect walk: quantum anomalous Hall effect. In a MnBi2Te4 or Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 micro-Hall cell at 2-10 K, magnetization sets which way the dissipationless edge channel circulates; read senses the Hall-voltage sign at sub-mV, and write uses the topological insulator's own giant spin-orbit torque.
why: Read dissipation approaches zero (quantized, backscatter-free), which matters where every nW at 4 K costs ~1 W at room temperature: >=10x lower system energy per access than shipping data to warm DRAM for quantum-control and cryo-compute stacks.
